Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "David Copperfield", "unit": 39, "heading": "CHAPTER 37. A LITTLE COLD WATER", "previous_rows": [{"source_id": "en85-u039-b0030", "target": "— Теперь я не ужасный, Дора? — спросил я нежно.", "source_sha256": "6a82bba196df0f8eab871b749dfa21c61584e6dcf2b37cd5903e17b91bc87e92", "target_id": "ru-en85-u039-b0030", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "7e2aeea6660a11b8d47411f7efb35a02fa0320026a7e2efb0ba59de92c007710"}, {"source_id": "en85-u039-b0031", "target": "— Ах, нет, нет! — воскликнула Дора. — Но я надеюсь, что твоя тётушка будет подолгу сидеть в своей комнате. И я надеюсь, что она не сварливая старуха!", "source_sha256": "07da5d92303df150fc6c1e8bb5f3ebaf87437a99b9866bd20958f8de65f41bc8", "target_id": "ru-en85-u039-b0031", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "13149943d8d388daf5d12fddae090905bc60fc03bcbe62b3225a1d836236a187"}], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 37, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u039-b0032", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "If it were possible for me to love Dora more than ever, I am sure I did. But I felt she was a little impracticable. It damped my new-born ardour, to find that ardour so difficult of communication to her. I made another trial. When she was quite herself again, and was curling Jip’s ears, as he lay upon her lap, I became grave, and said:", "sha256": "c34d31112a929916ff2874efb53d39f1666d106e43701d3009841324010dd447", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[32]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0033", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My own! May I mention something?’", "sha256": "fe6dd6e7322283e84bf80dfbb7bd5a473f9a1602f8bac11bc9fcfc3577714c2d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[33]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0034", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Oh, please don’t be practical!’ said Dora, coaxingly. ‘Because it frightens me so!’", "sha256": "d9a3b6602ecb78e9f7112a2fadf6e9a7a0fbbaf7f182eb854fd1328964bca6d2", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[34]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0035", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Sweetheart!’ I returned; ‘there is nothing to alarm you in all this. I want you to think of it quite differently. I want to make it nerve you, and inspire you, Dora!’", "sha256": "e84d981c1ad1ac60db7bd04a1e435f7a1bf58e2a0c58044773d8ba12ab29922e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[35]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0036", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Oh, but that’s so shocking!’ cried Dora.", "sha256": "6e95392511a5dbc609a3ff6da7ec118897c6aa4ddf53be1b185a2bb2d56b4fab", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[36]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0037", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My love, no. Perseverance and strength of character will enable us to bear much worse things.’ ‘But I haven’t got any strength at all,’ said Dora, shaking her curls. ‘Have I, Jip? Oh, do kiss Jip, and be agreeable!’", "sha256": "484e0c7a385e30d181b5f95cb1d18ae02a5377c691461cbe4980934028a23d05", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[37]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0038", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "It was impossible to resist kissing Jip, when she held him up to me for that purpose, putting her own bright, rosy little mouth into kissing form, as she directed the operation, which she insisted should be performed symmetrically, on the centre of his nose. I did as she bade me—rewarding myself afterwards for my obedience—and she charmed me out of my graver character for I don’t know how long.", "sha256": "d5e2056d7a0c7e8310ba81f0066a0168413c746b14ed4f7c42ee01d5e7fd5563", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[38]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0039", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘But, Dora, my beloved!’ said I, at last resuming it; ‘I was going to mention something.’", "sha256": "a3a85511ec6c89233a779eda1e7c3c24e50df9caf0012af93244b437c270c6d3", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[39]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0040", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "The judge of the Prerogative Court might have fallen in love with her, to see her fold her little hands and hold them up, begging and praying me not to be dreadful any more.", "sha256": "c8b71a531fa6b216593af711dddf45b2cfb2506d7440b602bf2baad5528c87ca", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[40]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0041", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Indeed I am not going to be, my darling!’ I assured her. ‘But, Dora, my love, if you will sometimes think,—not despondingly, you know; far from that!—but if you will sometimes think—just to encourage yourself—that you are engaged to a poor man—’", "sha256": "ad5bcee217d7e54ac498a4edd9b1327810e859088a10e894d4b0fddf0a30fc01", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[41]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0042", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Don’t, don’t! Pray don’t!’ cried Dora. ‘It’s so very dreadful!’", "sha256": "1a3c341151932350e8d8d7d20fa74947bc020dbea93f9cc9eee0574e87592624", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[42]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0043", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My soul, not at all!’ said I, cheerfully. ‘If you will sometimes think of that, and look about now and then at your papa’s housekeeping, and endeavour to acquire a little habit—of accounts, for instance—’", "sha256": "f29e800d4e90d963dbd8825c67cc567d8a4f226a4522d6f9719f37ef09edf100", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[43]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0044", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Poor little Dora received this suggestion with something that was half a sob and half a scream.", "sha256": "b41eac1aa2f1f91787683ca0eba02949d461880f0735012e3fe4345fb32d3606", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[44]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0045", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘—It would be so useful to us afterwards,’ I went on. ‘And if you would promise me to read a little—a little Cookery Book that I would send you, it would be so excellent for both of us. For our path in life, my Dora,’ said I, warming with the subject, ‘is stony and rugged now, and it rests with us to smooth it. We must fight our way onward. We must be brave. There are obstacles to be met, and we must meet, and crush them!’", "sha256": "0e6ad7fc18114a17c6eff3b1dde5d32b9c2c3b83f5472662489c08e41cb147b8", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[45]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0046", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I was going on at a great rate, with a clenched hand, and a most enthusiastic countenance; but it was quite unnecessary to proceed. I had said enough. I had done it again. Oh, she was so frightened! Oh, where was Julia Mills! Oh, take her to Julia Mills, and go away, please! So that, in short, I was quite distracted, and raved about the drawing-room.", "sha256": "7f81ec83c803705d2a3655721b4e08da0fe9a790dbe2bfd2fc2e8cf17dd1ad94", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[46]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0047", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I thought I had killed her, this time. I sprinkled water on her face. I went down on my knees. I plucked at my hair. I denounced myself as a remorseless brute and a ruthless beast. I implored her forgiveness. I besought her to look up. I ravaged Miss Mills’s work-box for a smelling-bottle, and in my agony of mind applied an ivory needle-case instead, and dropped all the needles over Dora. I shook my fists at Jip, who was as frantic as myself. I did every wild extravagance that could be done, and was a long way beyond the end of my wits when Miss Mills came into the room.", "sha256": "f6b5b4788cdb6ebb00a2cc257a82a29803c870cf7efd14d509a32be5bc6a3f07", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[47]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0048", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Who has done this?’ exclaimed Miss Mills, succouring her friend.", "sha256": "0a6fe1ec03977d0817ef900f04459882393d1f2e3ca23575ca3c6b97215df54e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[48]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0049", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I replied, ‘I, Miss Mills! I have done it! Behold the destroyer!’—or words to that effect—and hid my face from the light, in the sofa cushion.", "sha256": "471d471dfb1895539dfec7de4d52a97801ee7530b1a333c99284742806b312eb", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[49]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0050", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "At first Miss Mills thought it was a quarrel, and that we were verging on the Desert of Sahara; but she soon found out how matters stood, for my dear affectionate little Dora, embracing her, began exclaiming that I was ‘a poor labourer’; and then cried for me, and embraced me, and asked me would I let her give me all her money to keep, and then fell on Miss Mills’s neck, sobbing as if her tender heart were broken.", "sha256": "dc2b3fc1d99c6d361e7662db87ad9a4f0b7bd6bccd151f2a29e8f77644fc9d19", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[50]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0051", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Miss Mills must have been born to be a blessing to us. She ascertained from me in a few words what it was all about, comforted Dora, and gradually convinced her that I was not a labourer—from my manner of stating the case I believe Dora concluded that I was a navigator, and went balancing myself up and down a plank all day with a wheelbarrow—and so brought us together in peace. When we were quite composed, and Dora had gone up-stairs to put some rose-water to her eyes, Miss Mills rang for tea. In the ensuing interval, I told Miss Mills that she was evermore my friend, and that my heart must cease to vibrate ere I could forget her sympathy.", "sha256": "a9d15bbd49f1977f95b6277396a3f24f90e1c1e1a2b7a72d0300f4d2a5f6123f", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[51]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0052", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I then expounded to Miss Mills what I had endeavoured, so very unsuccessfully, to expound to Dora. Miss Mills replied, on general principles, that the Cottage of content was better than the Palace of cold splendour, and that where love was, all was.", "sha256": "7da83ca9b5374b4d29febae3b20e26e6ee2216d82d7417d16ed0bd42a36d087d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[52]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0053", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I said to Miss Mills that this was very true, and who should know it better than I, who loved Dora with a love that never mortal had experienced yet? But on Miss Mills observing, with despondency, that it were well indeed for some hearts if this were so, I explained that I begged leave to restrict the observation to mortals of the masculine gender.", "sha256": "6f6e1f8b0fa91f3f6cf96f1627597e58df0950f1a43beac31bcc9c62e1f8ab90", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[53]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0054", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I then put it to Miss Mills, to say whether she considered that there was or was not any practical merit in the suggestion I had been anxious to make, concerning the accounts, the housekeeping, and the Cookery Book?", "sha256": "91d824b69bc249781ad4f57d8205edad1323c62c53ef8d8bc2f04b2955f9799c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[54]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0055", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Miss Mills, after some consideration, thus replied:", "sha256": "5773d40667c4a972b31771e88b7fc775925abe65f4644191f8de2cd3ffd7c053", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[55]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0056", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Mr. Copperfield, I will be plain with you. Mental suffering and trial supply, in some natures, the place of years, and I will be as plain with you as if I were a Lady Abbess. No. The suggestion is not appropriate to our Dora. Our dearest Dora is a favourite child of nature. She is a thing of light, and airiness, and joy. I am free to confess that if it could be done, it might be well, but—’ And Miss Mills shook her head.", "sha256": "83a6cfaf4f1fce0cb589e6dda28bd68f143c3dcd545f099be96ba3e2f5fa98a3", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[56]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0057", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I was encouraged by this closing admission on the part of Miss Mills to ask her, whether, for Dora’s sake, if she had any opportunity of luring her attention to such preparations for an earnest life, she would avail herself of it? Miss Mills replied in the affirmative so readily, that I further asked her if she would take charge of the Cookery Book; and, if she ever could insinuate it upon Dora’s acceptance, without frightening her, undertake to do me that crowning service. Miss Mills accepted this trust, too; but was not sanguine.", "sha256": "5870b62dfb6c0c0c8e73337a543edcff2ad03a071b4ee3c2622f2fb2ef7496fd", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[57]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0058", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "And Dora returned, looking such a lovely little creature, that I really doubted whether she ought to be troubled with anything so ordinary. And she loved me so much, and was so captivating (particularly when she made Jip stand on his hind legs for toast, and when she pretended to hold that nose of his against the hot teapot for punishment because he wouldn’t), that I felt like a sort of Monster who had got into a Fairy’s bower, when I thought of having frightened her, and made her cry.", "sha256": "f530ae7dd3da2e943e286c4f1e6b52eb0357a15dc33470b1b1ecf526dd134f71", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[58]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0059", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "After tea we had the guitar; and Dora sang those same dear old French songs about the impossibility of ever on any account leaving off dancing, La ra la, La ra la, until I felt a much greater Monster than before.", "sha256": "fe2f2a54cc6c5ed802e1a8ecadfd7fa4cacda13a887a2ccce8d62b5088ba662e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[59]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0060", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "We had only one check to our pleasure, and that happened a little while before I took my leave, when, Miss Mills chancing to make some allusion to tomorrow morning, I unluckily let out that, being obliged to exert myself now, I got up at five o’clock. Whether Dora had any idea that I was a Private Watchman, I am unable to say; but it made a great impression on her, and she neither played nor sang any more.", "sha256": "67e87d6dd60fa0284a40186b753f2acce3d8611cb04584d6bd0a5575a8133912", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[60]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0061", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "It was still on her mind when I bade her adieu; and she said to me, in her pretty coaxing way—as if I were a doll, I used to think:", "sha256": "9c437521c870b6a96f2c22920a1e9826df56fb757c76d7ee1ede6cd81f36ab06", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[61]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0062", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Now don’t get up at five o’clock, you naughty boy. It’s so nonsensical!’", "sha256": "a9c1e851b963807eb95d991a3bb1341431bd0dd52cf0aaccddce92ba94076ce4", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[62]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u039-b0063", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My love,’ said I, ‘I have work to do.’", "sha256": "4ce4d94d0ab8d99848dfaecaf0e57fbfe94b9363db08f06f4aa09ff223791c1c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[44]/p[63]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}]}
